questions.prompt: Directions: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on what in their university impresses them most.You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.correctAnswer:
What impresses me most about my university is the atmosphere of shared learning in its library. The building is useful, but the people and habits within it make the place special to me.

When I first arrived, I struggled to find materials for a course project. A student volunteer showed me how to search the catalogue and compare different sources. Later, I noticed that classmates often exchanged reading suggestions while respecting the quiet study areas. Staff also offered short introductions to research resources, making unfamiliar tools less intimidating. These small forms of support encouraged me to ask better questions and study more independently.

The library represents a wider quality that I value in the university: knowledge is something to explore together rather than keep to oneself. I hope to contribute by helping new students as others helped me. This everyday spirit of cooperation has left a deeper impression than any single ceremony.

questions.hint: 题目是大学中最打动你的事物或特点，需要明确对象与理由。
questions.explanation:
以下为按题意独立写成的参考范文，作文没有唯一答案。选择图书馆合作学习氛围，用志愿者与资料指导举例，最后写愿意回馈；不能泛泛赞美大学。

选定图书馆学习氛围作为最深印象，第一段点题，主体用志愿者帮助和资料指导支持，结尾写获得帮助后愿意回馈。learning environment是学习环境，offer guidance是提供指导，give something back是作回馈。what…impresses要求清楚指出一个对象，再说明why；只说学校美丽、老师好会缺少中心。不要把该题写成大学简介，例子应展示自己如何感受到这种特点。

练习方法：先用提示列三段提纲，在30分钟内独立写作，再按下方标准逐项打分；把失分最多的一段重写。参考范文约152词（缩写、连字符词按一词，含标题或书信称呼落款），满足120–180词要求；评分用于练习自检，不代表官方阅卷分数。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：题目覆盖0–6＋结构0–4＋语言0–5，先独立写完再对照；观点不同于范文也可得满分，只要有合理支持。
题目覆盖0–6分：该题检查——题目是大学中最打动你的事物或特点，需要明确对象与理由。。6分=任务完整且有具体理由/活动/例证；4–5分=切题但细节偏薄；2–3分=遗漏主要任务；0–1分=基本离题。
结构0–4分：4分=开头明确任务、主体按逻辑展开、结尾回扣，段间自然；3分=顺序清楚但局部衔接生硬；1–2分=跳跃或机械罗列；0分=内容难以组织理解。
语言0–5分：5分=语法和用词基本准确、句型有变化；3–4分=少量错误但不影响理解；1–2分=反复出现时态、主谓一致或搭配错误并影响阅读；0分=多数句子不能理解。
格式与修订：按原题保持120–180词；新闻/书信/提案用对应体裁，明确要求的首句逐字保留。若超限、少写任务或缺必要格式，先修改再评分，不把字数达标当作内容满分。

questions.prompt: Research has found the use of digital technology benefits not only teenagers' social lives but also their studies.
questions.passage:
Teenagers and social networking

A) As a parent of two boys at primary school, I worry about the issues associated with teenagers and social media. Newspapers are constantly filled with frightening accounts of drug addiction and aggressive behaviour supposedly caused by violent video games. But even when these accounts touch on real concerns, they do not really reflect the great mass of everyday teenage social behaviour: the online chat, the texting, the surfing, and the emergence of a new teenage sphere that is conducted digitally.

B) New technologies always provoke generational panic, which usually has more to do with adult fears than with the lives of teenagers. In the 1930s, parents worried that radio was gaining "an irresistible hold of their children". In the 80s, the great danger was the Sony Walkman(随身听). When you look at today's digital activity, the facts are much more positive than you might expect.

C) Indeed, social scientists who study young people have found that their digital use can be inventive and even beneficial. This is true not just in terms of their social lives, but their education too. So if you use a ton of social media, do you become unable, or unwilling, to engage in face-to-face contact? The evidence suggests not. Research by Amanda Lenhart of the Pew Research Centre, a US think tank, found that the most passionate texters are also the kids most likely to spend time with friends in person. One form of socialising doesn't replace the other. It expands it.

In the history of horse racing, few horses have captured the affection of the British public like Red Rum. Today, three decades after his retirement, he is still one of the best-known and most beloved racehorses of all time.

He was 12 years old and not expected to place highly. The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you. In these situations, instincts can help you make effective and quick decisions.
